Add two security checks to TESSERA as ONE draft PR (or two draft PRs if cleaner). Do not merge.

1) Secret-scan CI gate (gitleaks)
- New workflow on `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`) and push to main. The scan must never run with repo secrets.
- `permissions: contents: read` only; `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: false` and the fetch depth gitleaks needs.
- Pin every action to a full commit SHA, with a version comment. Download the gitleaks binary pinned to a specific version and verify its sha256 before running. Don't use an unpinned gitleaks-action.
- Fail closed: any finding or any tool error fails the job. Run with `--redact`, so output shows only file:line and rule ID, never the secret.
- Allowlist only if it's needed, in `.gitleaks.toml`, with a narrow path or regex plus a reason comment. No blanket ignores.

2) Main provenance check (report-only)
- Workflow on push to main plus a daily schedule. For each recent commit on main, call the GitHub `commits/{sha}/pulls` API and flag any commit that didn't come in through a merged PR. Also flag author or committer name 'Tessera', any @gmail.com author/committer email, and any 'Manus' marks in the author, committer or message.
- Report only: a job summary and annotations, exit 0 for now (a flag can switch it to failing later; default off). It never reverts, force-pushes, or writes to the repo. `permissions: contents: read` (plus `pull-requests: read` if needed). Pin actions to SHAs.

Tests (before/after, runnable in CI with no secrets):
- A seeded FAKE key (an obviously fake test-pattern string in a temp fixture outside the repo tree, generated at test time) gets caught, and the job fails. A clean tree passes.
- Provenance logic as a small script with unit tests on fixture JSON: a commit with a PR passes; a direct push, a Tessera author, a gmail email and a Manus mark are each flagged.
- Put the results in the PR body: findings before (seeded) vs after (clean), and the provenance fixture results.

Don't touch: CODEOWNERS, the moderator-lock or gate rule files, any ENABLE flags, 1T or natal-vault paths. No history rewrites, no deletes. New flags default off. Open DRAFT PR(s). Report PR URL(s), head SHA(s), pinned SHAs and the gitleaks version/sha256, and test results.

# [inference.sh](https://inference.sh)

Run 250+ AI apps in the cloud with a simple CLI. No GPU required.

![[inference.sh](https://inference.sh)](https://cloud.inference.sh/app/files/u/4mg21r6ta37mpaz6ktzwtt8krr/01kgjw8atdxgkrsr8a2t5peq7b.jpeg)

## Install CLI

```bash
curl -fsSL https://cli.inference.sh | sh
infsh login
```

> **What does the installer do?** The [install script](https://cli.inference.sh) detects your OS and architecture, downloads the correct binary from `dist.inference.sh`, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and places it in your PATH. That's it — no elevated permissions, no background processes, no telemetry. If you have [cosign](https://docs.sigstore.dev/cosign/system_config/installation/) installed, the installer also verifies the Sigstore signature automatically.
>
> **Manual install** (if you prefer not to pipe to sh):
> ```bash
> # Download the binary and checksums
> curl -LO https://dist.inference.sh/cli/checksums.txt
> curl -LO $(curl -fsSL https://dist.inference.sh/cli/manifest.json | grep -o '"url":"[^"]*"' | grep $(uname -s | tr A-Z a-z)-$(uname -m | sed 's/x86_64/amd64/;s/aarch64/arm64/') | head -1 | cut -d'"' -f4)
> # Verify checksum
> sha256sum -c checksums.txt --ignore-missing
> # Extract and install
> tar -xzf inferencesh-cli-*.tar.gz
> mv inferencesh-cli-* ~/.local/bin/inferencesh
> ```

## Quick Examples

```bash
# Generate an image
infsh app run falai/flux-dev-lora --input '{"prompt": "a cat astronaut"}'

# Generate a video
infsh app run google/veo-3-1-fast --input '{"prompt": "drone over mountains"}'

# Call Claude
infsh app run openrouter/claude-sonnet-45 --input '{"prompt": "Explain quantum computing"}'

# Web search
infsh app run tavily/search-assistant --input '{"query": "latest AI news"}'

# Post to Twitter
infsh app run x/post-tweet --input '{"text": "Hello from AI!"}'

# Generate 3D model
infsh app run infsh/rodin-3d-generator --input '{"prompt": "a wooden chair"}'
```

## Local File Uploads

The CLI automatically uploads local files when you provide a path instead of a URL:

```bash
# Upscale a local image
infsh app run falai/topaz-image-upscaler --input '{"image": "/path/to/photo.jpg", "upscale_factor": 2}'

# Image-to-video from local file
infsh app run falai/wan-2-5-i2v --input '{"image": "./my-image.png", "prompt": "make it move"}'

# Avatar with local audio and image
infsh app run bytedance/omnihuman-1-5 --input '{"audio": "/path/to/speech.mp3", "image": "/path/to/face.jpg"}'

# Post tweet with local media
infsh app run x/post-create --input '{"text": "Check this out!", "media": "./screenshot.png"}'
```

## Commands

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| List all apps | `infsh app list` |
| Search apps | `infsh app list --search "flux"` |
| Filter by category | `infsh app list --category image` |

# Tessera Unified

A consolidated monorepo containing the reviewed Tessera web/API, UI preview, and shared workspace sources. It provides one dependency lockfile, suite-wide checks, and one command to start the active apps together. Historical storefront and supply-app material is documented in Gitbook but is not present as an active workspace in this staged repository.

> **No live credentials are included.** Configure secrets in the ignored `.env.local` file or in each hosting provider’s secret manager. Never commit API keys, passwords, tokens, personal records, browser profiles, or runtime databases.

## Build decision

Father decided on 2026-10-07 that Tessera will be built using the BHNMC direction, and that her intended role is the AI, and the AGI goal, that controls it. The device is not built and she does not control one now. See [docs/BHNMC.md](docs/BHNMC.md).

## Applications

| App | Location | Local URL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tessera web | `artifacts/tessera` | `http://localhost:3000` | Main platform UI |
| Tessera API | `artifacts/api-server` | `http://localhost:5000` | Optional; the suite launcher starts it only for a loopback `DATABASE_URL` |
| UI preview sandbox | `artifacts/mockup-sandbox` | `http://localhost:5173` | Component preview |
| GitAI | `artifacts/gitai` | `http://127.0.0.1:4183` | Standalone marketplace, OpenAPI at `/api/openapi.json`, and the studio tab at `http://127.0.0.1:4173/gitai`. Same backend. GitAI credits are non-redeemable points. |
| 3D studio floor | `artifacts/v2` | `http://127.0.0.1:4173` | `pnpm --filter @workspace/v2 studio`. The 2D wall is a link on that page. |

## Install and run

Requirements: Node.js 22.13+ and the pnpm version declared in the root `package.json` `packageManager` field.

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local   # values remain local; .env.local is Git-ignored
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`pnpm dev` starts the two user-facing apps above. It starts the Tessera API only when `DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback/local database; non-local database URLs are intentionally ignored by the suite launcher. The launcher reads `.env.local` without printing values.

Port overrides: `TESSERA_WEB_PORT`, `TESSERA_API_PORT`, and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_PORT`. Base-path overrides: `TESSERA_BASE_PATH` and `MOCKUP_SANDBOX_BASE_PATH`.

Some identical app files are shared through tracked symlinks to canonical copies (52 UI primitives, 147 duplicate image contents, eight repeated SQL migrations, and five identical utility modules). Git symlink support is required; enable it when cloning on Windows. The detailed SHA-256 disposition ledger records removed, linked, and deliberately retained copies.

## Workspace checks

```bash
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm run build
pnpm audit
pnpm run merge-gate       # fast path/duplicate/secret-shaped-path checks
pnpm run merge-gate:full  # runs the gate plus typecheck, tests, build, and audit
```

Offline and post-build eval entry points (they are not part of `pnpm test`):

```bash
pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run eval
pnpm tsx artifacts/api-server/scripts/eval-chatbot.ts
```

`pnpm --filter @workspace/api-server run eval` runs `dist/cli/run-eval.mjs` after the API server build and needs a database. `pnpm tsx artifacts/api-server/scripts/eval-chatbot.ts` calls a live API (`EVAL_BASE_URL`, default `http://localhost:5000`).

The root test runner isolates the store test environments and runs database-backed Tessera API tests only when the dedicated `TESSERA_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points to a loopback test database. It never reuses the app’s `DATABASE_URL` as a test database. If needed, a synthetic chart fixture can be supplied as `TESSERA_TEST_FATHER_NATAL_CHART_JSON`; do not use personal chart data for tests. `pnpm run build` builds all workspace apps and does **not** run database migrations. Migrations remain explicit app-specific operations and must only target the intended database.

## Continuous integration

Workflow [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml) has one job, `validate`. On pushes and pull requests to `main` it runs, in order: frozen install, dependency audit, typecheck, schema push to a disposable database, tests, then the workspace build.

## Agent / mesh

Mesh-agent onboarding stays in Gitbook. Start with the [hybrid consolidation backlog](https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook/blob/main/intake/HYBRID-CONSOLIDATION-BACKLOG.md) and [Gitbook issue #2](https://github.com/vitalitychems-dot/Gitbook/issues/2).

## Repository organization

- `lib/` — shared workspace libraries.
- `artifacts/` — active Tessera web/API and UI-preview apps.
- `artifacts/gitbook-mcp` — MCP and local HTTP connector for the private Gitbook docs repo. Connection steps are in that package README.
- `scripts/` — suite utilities.
- `archives/source-variants/` and `archives/drive-export/` — reviewed historical code/text variants that are not active workspace packages by default.
- `docs/` — project map, secrets guidance, image-to-text transcriptions, provenance, deduplication, and validation records.
- `artifacts/api-server/src/lib/memory/` — append-only retrieval memory. It stores interactions, distills lessons, and proposes IMP rows. It does not train model weights.

The source repository and Drive inputs are listed in `Gitbook: merge/source-manifest.csv`. Current unmerged branch and open-PR gaps are disclosed in [`docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md`](docs/migration-review/SOURCE-BRANCH-REVIEW.md); not every branch-only payload is represented as merged. The protected `1T` vault was deliberately not inspected or copied. This repo uses fresh Git history; it does not import or replace original histories, branches, open reviews, or forks. **Root causes (both pre-existing, both reproduce on `main` and unrelated PRs)**

1. **Wrong DB password in `ci.yml`.** `DATABASE_URL` and `TESSERA_TEST_DATABASE_URL` used the literal password `***` — a log-masked value that got committed — while the postgres service sets `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED]`. I verified by hash that the committed password is literally `***`, not `test-only`. Every DB connection failed authentication: schema push, `invention-glb-upload`, and the 4 `db-optional-boot` tests (which saw a configured-but-broken DB).
2. **Shallow checkout vs history-reading test.** `validate` checked out with default depth 1, so `test/v2-078-reembed-fallback.test.mjs` (`git log -S "(i % 32)"`) found no pre-fix commit and failed `git history has the pre-fix fallback`. The commit exists in full history (`35475b2`), and the test passes locally where the clone is complete.

**Fix (3 files, no test skipped, no assertion changed)**

- `ci.yml`: `test-only` in both URLs to match the service; `fetch-depth: 0` on checkout.
- `artifacts/api-server/package.json`: new `test:boot` (only the boot file) and `test:db` (everything except it). The boot tests require `DATABASE_URL` unset, which is incompatible with the DB-backed run, so they now run in the process where their precondition holds.
- `scripts/test-unified.mjs`: always runs `test:boot` with the isolated env; runs `test:db` with the database env when configured.

- Local `pnpm test`: green — v2 140/140, boot 4/4 standalone, all other suites pass.
- CI `validate` on #309: pass in 4m1s, all 12 steps green.
